text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- The government coalition is split over plans to introduce road-pricing for trucks on Austrian highways. Conservative Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner says Austria cannot make the move on its own, while the dominant Social Democrats accuse him of trying to postpone the decision.
- The paper says President Thomas Klestil admitted in a 1989 interview that he knew about Iran's involvement in the affair surrounding the alleged murder of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna.
- Austrian farmers will have to start paying taxes on earnings not directly related to their farming activity.
- Federal railways monopoly OeBB plans to raise short distance fares to compensate for higher costs.
- Austrian Energy, a subsidiary of engineering group VA Technologie, said 1996 sales rose to 5.6 billion schillings from 3.1 billion a year earlier.
- Tourism stagnated this winter, but the government expects a slight improvement in the current year.

- Austrian central bank chief Klaus Liebscher says he is unimpressed by the European Commission's forecast that Italy will not qualify for monetary union, says the final decision will be made in 1997.
- Oberbank, a regional subsidiary of Creditanstalt, will keep its 1996 dividend steady at 13 schillings.
DIE PRESSE
- NATO is refusing to speed up talks on Austrian membership in the defence alliance, saying the country should first decide itself whether it wants to join or not.

- Central bank chief Klaus Liebscher says Austria will be among the first members of European monetary union. He called on the country's labour unions to take part in the government's information campaign on the euro.
- Vienna's airport charges the highest airport fees in all of Europe. Now the EU plans to standardize the fees across the union.
- Federal railways OeBB will have to pay 640 million schillings a year in communal taxes after Austria's high court abolished its tax exemption.
- Ski jumper Andreas Goldberger says he will fight against allegations of repeated drug abuse.

- Building society s-Bausparkasse, which has exclusive rights to sell its saving contracts through Bank Austria, wants to start selling its contracts through Creditanstalt as well. Bank Austria took a majority stake in Creditanstalt earlier this year.
- Builder Illbau is looking for a strategic partner, talks are underway with France's Bouyges and Germany's Bilfinger.
- Carton maker Mayr-Melnhof says business in the next few months will be "very good" after reporting limp set of first-quarter earnings.
KURIER
- Former Justice Minister Foregger is alleged to have given false information to parliament in 1989 during a parliamentary debate about the alleged murder of three Kurdish leaders in Vienna in 1989.
- Airline owner and former Formula One champion Niki Lauda underwent an operation in a Vienna hospital to receive a new kidney.
- Herzmansky, one of Vienna's most traditional department stores, to close this summer. German textile chain Peek & Cloppenburg will take over the downtown Vienna premises next year.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Fibremaker Lenzing is expected to close down its loss-making U.S. plant.
